$comment: THE single greppable source of truth for every version the Alpha Windows
installer downloads. Nothing else may pin a version: installer/bootstrap.ps1,
installer/lib/Alpha.Installer.psm1, .devcontainer/devcontainer.json and
build/compose.installer.yaml all read this file (or are asserted against it by
installer/tests/test_installer_contract.py).
repo.ref MUST be an immutable tag. A branch name here makes every released
install unreproducible, which is the exact failure the owner forbade.
NAMED CHANNELS, strictly additive to repo.ref. repo.ref is UNCHANGED and
stays the immutable release pin that
test_pinned_repository_ref_is_a_tag_not_a_moving_branch guards. A moving
ref must NEVER be written into repo.ref: that test rejects it by design,
and it is correct to do so.
Why channels exist: the repository had ZERO tags, so repo.ref=v2.1.0
resolved to nothing and the installer failed at the clone step on every
run. The fix is NOT to weaken repo.ref to 'main'. It is an immutable
v2.1.0 tag PLUS a moving 'stable' tag, so a single installer always
yields the newest release without giving up the ability to pin one.
default - what bootstrap.ps1 uses when -Channel is not supplied.
stable  - a MOVING tag, force-advanced at each release, so one installer
always gives users the newest good build. This is the channel
that answers the owner's request for an installer that needs no
version bump to deliver updates.
pinned  - the exact release, for reproducing one user's specific bug.
main    - the moving branch, opt-in via -Channel main. NEVER the
default: it is unreproducible and can be caught mid-edit, which
would break the uv/node/pnpm pairings this file exists to hold.
REPRODUCIBILITY OF A MOVING CHANNEL: because 'stable' does not identify
one commit over time, bootstrap.ps1 records the RESOLVED COMMIT SHA into
the install manifest at install time. Every individual install therefore
remains traceable to an exact commit, and that commit stays reachable
either by SHA or by its immutable vX.Y.Z tag. Moving the channel costs
the pin, not the ability to reproduce an install.

uv.$comment: MUST equal backend/Dockerfile's UV_IMAGE tag. backend/tests/test_ci_uv_version_pin.py enforces that pairing for CI; installer/tests/test_installer_contract.py enforces it for the installer.

python.$comment: Minor series only. uv resolves the exact patch, so the installer never hardcodes a patch that can rot.

node.$comment: MUST equal electron/desktop-config.json nodeVersion. The frontend is a Next.js SERVER (next start), so a Node runtime is required at runtime; there is no static bundle.

packageManager.$comment: MUST equal the root package.json packageManager field.

requirements.$comment: 19041 = Windows 10 2004. WebView2 Evergreen is guaranteed present from Windows 11 and Windows 10 1803+; 19041 is the floor where the whole stack is supported.

defaults.$comment: SQLite so no database server is required. Postgres is opt-in via -WithPostgres.
